answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that deposit when an audited task is proven fraudulent. A glacier of duplicated accounts is no longer cheap: every sybil ties up capital, and coordinated fakes risk losing it. Deposits alone cannot stop a wealthy attacker, so caps on influence per stake and public audits help keep a reef of honest agents from being drowned out; yarrow can be the name of the audit pool, not a security guarantee.
